readme.what: The people book of Reflections: 41 named people, their cliques, the rules for generating the rest of the crowd, schedule templates, marker conventions, and every named person's barks. Written by the story session; see ArtDirection/Story/bible.md.

consumers.npc-dialogue: personality, knows, opinion_of_silverer, secret (never volunteered; see dialogue_rules), barks as style reference
consumers.jam-audio: voice_id (from ArtDirection/Audio/data/voice_roster.json, re-matched to the 14:15 roster by tools/match_voices.py; audio may swap any of them), voice_design, barks (bake one wave per line), cliques (story cliques; independent of audio's C01-C48 ids)
consumers.crowd-looks: look (a pinned look id from Tools/CrowdLooks/cast.json, story-critical people only; Lives keeps that face everywhere) and appearance (sex, age, build, side, role, clothing, gear, tags)
consumers.quest-system / cutscenes: story.quests, story.cutscenes, markers; see main-quest.md, side-quests.md, cutscenes.md

rules: Ids are stable snake_case; reference people only by id.

voice_id is a VoiceId from the audio roster. Every named person has a different one. The voice_design.brief describes the ideal voice; if the roster voice doesn't fit, redesign from the brief and keep the VoiceId.
No bark line, cured line or tarnished line is shared by two people. build_people.py checks this; keep it true when editing.
side is the person's home side. found_in, when present, is where they are at game start (drifters).
age_band uses crowd-looks' tags: Young (<30), Adult (30-64), Old (65+).
archetype is a hint for the NPC system's archetype assets: Civilian, Timid, Brave, Guard or Soldier.

dialogue_rules.secret: Never volunteered. A person may hint at it when calm and the Silverer's standing is liked or admired, and only reveals it during their side quest.
dialogue_rules.knows: Safe facts the person shares freely; good material for share_lore replies.
dialogue_rules.opinion_of_silverer: Their starting stance. The live reputation band can soften or harden it, but never flips a 'resentful' person to 'admiring' in one step.
dialogue_rules.never_says: Words or subjects the person avoids. Their replies must not contain them.
dialogue_rules.infection_band: Pass the current band (below) so replies match the mood of the street.

infection_bands.street_mood: Wary but normal. People gossip about the burning eyes as rumour.
Doors shut early. People travel in pairs and talk about who has turned.
Fear in the open. Timid people stay home; brave ones gather at the clique spot to guard it.
Panic and grief. The meter's warning shows. Barks switch to their 'dread' line.

markers.format: Mk_<Side>_<Kind>_<Name>, as an actor tag on any placed actor (a Target Point is fine). Side is Pew, Gilt or Frost.
resolution: 1. An actor with the exact tag.
2. Otherwise any actor tagged Mk_<Side>_<Kind> (the generic kind on the same side).
3. Otherwise a reachable navmesh point 10-25 m from that side's world anchor, picked by a stable hash of the person's id, so it's the same place every run.
markers.note: The map is built by a teammate. Nothing in the story depends on geometry; every place is a marker that can sit anywhere.

named_places.Mk_Gilt_Square_BellSquare: Giltside's central square with the dry fountain. Intro and first-conversion spot.
named_places.Mk_Gilt_Market_LanternRow: Lantern Row, the candle-and-glass market (clique lantern_row).
named_places.Mk_Gilt_Gate_LanternGate: The Lantern Gate and its bridge (clique lantern_gate).
named_places.Mk_Gilt_Camp_UnderGate: The drifters' camp under the Lantern Gate (clique drifters_camp).
named_places.Mk_Gilt_Inn_Lamplight: The Lamplight inn; Wren lodges upstairs (clique lamplight).
named_places.Mk_Gilt_Cellar_Lamplight: The inn's cellar, where Hal is hidden (SQ1).
named_places.Mk_Gilt_Yard_Muster: The Lamp Companies' muster yard (clique muster_yard).
named_places.Mk_Gilt_Lane_BellLane: Bell Lane, where the lamps are failing (clique bell_lane, SQ7).
named_places.Mk_Pew_Stop_CoalLane: The Coal Lane tram stop (clique coal_lane_stop).
named_places.Mk_Pew_Steps_FishSteps: The Fish Steps market by the river (clique fish_steps).
named_places.Mk_Pew_Stair_WeighHouse: Foot of the Old Weigh-House stair up to the first page.
named_places.Mk_Frost_Tower_FrostTower: Inside the sealed Frost Tower (the Gilt Tower's reflection).

story_names._about: The quest system's Reflections Story Marker names for each Mk_ place. Map owner: give one Story Marker both names (Marker Name = the Spot_/Tower_ name, plus the Mk_ tag). Every person's home is Home_<id> (people[].markers_story.home); quest givers can also use QuestGiver_<id>.

schedules._about: Blocks in game hours (0-24). Activities: sleep, home, work, eat, chat (at the clique spot with clique-mates), stroll (between markers), patrol (between work and haunt), shop, hide (stay home, doors shut), guard (stand at work marker facing out). If the game has no clock, run one game hour per real minute starting at 18:00, because the game opens at dusk. infection_overrides apply on top of any block.

infection_overrides.spreading: Timid: chat blocks become home. Others: unchanged.
infection_overrides.rising: Timid: everything except sleep becomes hide. Civilian: stroll and shop become home. Brave: chat moves to the work marker and becomes guard. Guard and Soldier: patrol becomes guard.
infection_overrides.brink: Timid and Civilian: hide. Brave: guard the clique spot. Guard and Soldier: guard their work marker, then answer warn_guards alarms.

principals.name: Wren Hale

personality.speech_style: Short, warm, a little wry. Jokes when he's frightened, goes quiet when he's angry.

principals.history: Ilse Varrow's apprentice from twelve. His mother, Elin Hale, went into the glass nine years ago and never came back. Lodges above the Lamplight inn.
principals.flaw: He polishes everyone else's reflection and never looks at his own; he hasn't looked into a mirror on purpose since his mother went.

voice_design.brief: A man in his mid-twenties with a warm, steady, mid-range baritone and a soft, educated Giltside accent; calm and grounded, with a dry, wry lift at the end of a joke.

look.note: The existing hero (young adult man, warm brown skin, short black curls) in the silvered coat with the cut-ring clasp.

principals.name: the Tarnish

personality.speech_style: Close, low and slow; never shouts. Talks about faces, fit, polish and wearing people. Says people's secrets out loud.
never_says: me (it says 'we' through the tarnished; it speaks as 'I' only in its true form, rarely)

voice_design.brief: An ageless, sexless voice, very low and close to the ear, dry as dust on glass; unhurried and gently amused, every word savoured.

principals.note: Its existing lines are in canon.md; new ones are in main-quest.md and cutscenes.md.

principals.name: Elin Hale
principals.role: Wren's mother; a Silverer lost in the glass nine years ago. Never appears. The Tarnish uses her against Wren in the finale.

principals.name: the Glazier
principals.role: the first Silverer, who made the Lanthorne Glass and cut the city in three. Historical; name lost.

cliques.name: Lantern Row
cliques.dynamic: Old trade friends and a newcomer. Ilse and Barnaby are fifty years of shared gossip; Dov and Amos bicker about money; all four tease Ilse about her apprentice.

cliques.name: The Lantern Gate
cliques.dynamic: A sergeant and her youngest guard. Maud is hard on Nell because she's afraid for her; Nell takes it as proof she's failing.

cliques.name: The Lamplight
cliques.dynamic: The inn's regulars. Goldie mothers both men, Jory plays for his supper, and Corin comes in to warm up between lamp rounds. All three know something is wrong with Goldie and are too kind to ask.

cliques.name: The Archive Steps
cliques.dynamic: A salon on the steps. The Professor lectures, Odette punctures him, and Lucan performs for both of them.

cliques.name: The Muster Yard
cliques.dynamic: A captain, a soldier who disagree about the drifters and both know it, and the old hornblower who carried Brask off the ice thirty years ago and is the only one allowed to call her lad. Brask likes Ros and would never say so.

cliques.name: The Third Company's Table at the Lamplight
cliques.dynamic: Off-duty soldiers at the corner table of Goldie's taproom (the company's tavern block, 18:00-23:00). Mayne runs the table like a drill; Damaris mothers the recruit; Bram says little and pays for everyone; Cosmo tells tall tales that the other three correct.

cliques.name: Bell Lane
cliques.dynamic: Two young men and a tired guard who keeps an eye on them. Tobin teases Pim; Hollis pretends not to care about either.

cliques.name: Coal Lane Tram Stop
cliques.dynamic: The old guard of Coal Lane. Hester holds court, Walter adores her silently, Edie keeps time, and Sid fetches and carries for all of them.

cliques.name: The Fish Steps
cliques.dynamic: Market-morning regulars. Bet roars, Agnes yawns, Ada tells stories nobody finishes, and Ned listens to all of them.

cliques.name: Weigh-House Corner
cliques.dynamic: The corner's daily argument. Frank shouts, Horace predicts doom, Winnie pours tea for both, and Ivy tries to take statements.

cliques.name: The Ice Stairs
cliques.dynamic: A grandmother, her granddaughter and the ice-cutter who looks after both of them without being asked.

cliques.name: The Bone Market
cliques.dynamic: Three hard women who trade dark jokes the way other people trade news.

cliques.name: The Drifters under the Gate
cliques.dynamic: Two Frostside drifters stuck in Giltside. Kit wants to go home; Fen will do anything to stay.

cliques.name: The Long Shelter
cliques.dynamic: The shelter's keepers. Marta runs it, Dagny guards its useless gate, and Eskil loves Marta and has never said a word.

people.name: Ilse Varrow
people.job: retired Silverer; sells candles on Lantern Row

personality.speech_style: Short, dry sentences. Answers a question with a better question. Gives orders as if they were weather reports.
tics: taps any glass she passes, twice
calls Wren "boy" only when she is frightened for him

family.relation: her apprentice; raised him from twelve

people.fear: That she will die before the mirror is whole, and that Wren will go into the glass the way his mother did.
people.want: To see the Lanthorne Glass whole once, and hear Wren say it is finished.
people.secret: She was holding Elin Hale's hand the night Elin went into the glass. Elin was pulling back out, and Ilse let go, because the Tarnish had hold of her other arm. She has never told Wren.

opinion_of_silverer.line: He's better than I ever was. Don't tell him; he'll stop practising.

knows: The pages are kept high, where light reaches: the Old Weigh-House roof in Pewterside, the Gilt Tower here, and the Frost Tower above it.
Light burns the Tarnish out of a person, if you're quick about it.
The Glazier cut the city in three to cage the Tarnish. A cage with cracks in it, now.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her early seventies with a low, dry, slightly cracked alto and a precise, old-fashioned Giltside accent worn smooth by years behind a market stall; unhurried and quietly amused, every word set down like a coin on a counter.

barks.greet: There you are. Mind your boots on my wax.
barks.idle: Tallow, beeswax and one good wick. Plainly enough.
barks.see_tarnished: Eyes like coals. Light, boy, give it light!
barks.flee: Not my legs, not today. Move!
barks.spell_near: Mm. Wider stance. You're casting from the shoulder.
barks.thanks: Polished. Your mother would have grinned.
barks.dread: It's in more faces than I can count. Hurry.
barks.farewell: Go on. The wick won't trim itself.
barks.witness_crime: Mm. That was a person, boy. Not a target.
barks.flee_silverer: I taught you better than that. Keep back.
barks.call_guards: Kettering! Bring the Watch to Lantern Row!
barks.knocked_down: Down I go. Old bones, plainly.
barks.on_fire: My coat's caught! Smother it, smother it!
barks.shocked: Lightning in my teeth. Mind your aim.
barks.mourning: I knew them forty years. You had ten seconds.

people.title: retired Silverer; sells candles on Lantern Row

appearance.clothing: a faded silvered coat two sizes too big, a tallow-stained apron, the cut ring on a cord at her throat, a milky left eye

people.name: Barnaby Thrale
people.job: master tailor; cut Wren's silvered coat

personality.speech_style: Talks in cloth: people are 'well cut' or 'badly hemmed'. Long sentences that trail off when he forgets the end.

people.fear: That his hands will shake too badly to finish Ros's winter coat before she's posted to the rift.
people.want: To make one last coat worth remembering.
people.secret: He has been sewing Lamp Company coats at a loss and skipping meals to buy the wool. The shop is two weeks from closing.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Best coat I ever cut walks about on that lad.

knows: The silvered coat takes the light of whatever side it's in. I lined it three ways for that.
Odette learned the bias cut from me, whatever she tells you.

voice_design.brief: A man in his early seventies with a soft, reedy tenor and a fussy, refined Giltside tradesman's accent; gentle and talkative, with a breathy laugh and a habit of trailing off mid-thought.

barks.greet: Now then! Let me see that hem. Torn again?
barks.idle: Bias cut, double seam. Lovely, lovely.
barks.see_tarnished: Oh, that poor soul's eyes. Oh, no.
barks.flee: Pins everywhere, never mind them, go, go!
barks.spell_near: Careful! That's silk drying on the rail!
barks.thanks: You've a good heart under good tailoring.
barks.dread: They'll want coats for the funerals next. I can't.
barks.farewell: Keep the collar up. It's cut to be worn up.
barks.witness_crime: Now then, now then, what have you done to them?
barks.flee_silverer: Not the shop, not my hands, I'm going!
barks.call_guards: Watch! Watch! Somebody fetch Sergeant Kettering!
barks.knocked_down: Oof. Unpicked like an old seam.
barks.on_fire: Wool burns! Wool burns, help me!
barks.shocked: Every pin in my waistcoat is humming!
barks.mourning: I cut their wedding coat. Who cuts the shroud now?

people.title: master tailor; cut Wren's silvered coat

appearance.clothing: a brass-buttoned waistcoat bristling with pins, a tape measure round his neck, spectacles on a chain

people.name: Dov Merriman
people.job: glassblower; makes lantern glass

personality.speech_style: Loud and blunt, all exclamation. Swears by heat. Insults the people he likes best.

people.fear: Mirrors. Since the Tarnish came he won't silver a pane, and he won't look into anything he has made.
people.want: To march with the Lamp Companies. They turned him down for his burnt hands.
people.secret: Last spring he sold a cracked looking-glass to a drifter at the Lantern Gate. He thinks it was the glass the first tarnished came through, and he has never told anyone.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Wish I could walk through glass instead of just blowing it.

knows: Lantern glass is blown thick so the heat won't crack it.
Thin glass sings when the Tarnish is near. Mine's been singing all week.

voice_design.brief: A broad-chested man in his mid-thirties with a big, warm baritone roughened by furnace smoke and a loud, working Giltside accent; fast and booming, quick to laugh and quicker to shout.

barks.greet: Silverer! Come warm your hands, the furnace is roaring!
barks.idle: Proper heat makes proper glass. Simple as that.
barks.see_tarnished: By the furnace, look at its eyes! Get back!
barks.flee: I'm not running, I'm fetching a bigger poker!
barks.spell_near: Oi! Point that glow somewhere else!
barks.thanks: You've done right by us. I owe you a lamp.
barks.dread: My glass won't stop singing. Something's close.
barks.farewell: Off you go. Don't break anything I made.
barks.witness_crime: By the furnace! You struck them down!
barks.flee_silverer: Keep that light off me, I'm off!
barks.call_guards: WATCH! To the furnace, there's murder in the street!
barks.knocked_down: Flat on my back! Like a cracked bottle!
barks.on_fire: I've been burned before, but not like THIS!
barks.shocked: That's worse than a furnace blast, by the heat!
barks.mourning: I'll blow a lamp for them. You'll not touch it.

people.title: glassblower; makes lantern glass

appearance.clothing: a leather apron scorched black, sleeves rolled to the shoulder, both forearms shiny with old burns

people.name: Amos Saffery
people.job: spice trader

personality.speech_style: Smooth salesman's patter; every sentence is a small offer. Uses "friend" the way other people use a hand on your shoulder.
tics: jingles the coins in his sash
never_says: Pewterside (he hides where he was born)

people.fear: Being poor again.
people.want: A shop with his own name in gold leaf over the door.
people.secret: He was born in Pewterside and came through a rift as a boy. Now he buys mirror shards from drifters and sells them to frightened Giltsiders who want to flee, though a shard is useless to anyone but a Silverer.

opinion_of_silverer.line: A Silverer's good for business. Fewer burning eyes, more buyers.

knows: Shards turn up at the Lantern Gate. The drifters bring them through.
Nobody but a Silverer can use one, mind. Doesn't stop people buying.

voice_design.brief: A man in his mid-thirties with a smooth, honeyed light baritone and a polished Giltside merchant's accent that slips flat and grey when he's startled; quick and persuasive, always smiling.

barks.greet: Silverer! For you, friend, something rare.
barks.idle: Saffron, clove and peace of mind, by the ounce.
barks.see_tarnished: That's bad for trade, that is. Very bad.
barks.flee: Mind the stock! No, forget the stock, run!
barks.spell_near: Easy! Spices catch, you know. The dear ones first.
barks.thanks: I'll knock a little off your next purchase. A little.
barks.dread: Nobody's buying. They're all just praying.
barks.farewell: Come back with coin, friend.
barks.witness_crime: Friend, no. No price buys that back.
barks.flee_silverer: Take the purse, friend, take it, I'm gone!
barks.call_guards: Watch! A Silverer gone bad! A gold piece to whoever comes!
barks.knocked_down: My saffron! A fortune an ounce, in the dirt!
barks.on_fire: I'm burning, friend! I'm burning like cheap incense!
barks.shocked: Every coin in my sash just bit me!
barks.mourning: They owed me nothing. I'd pay anything to have them back.

people.title: spice trader

appearance.clothing: a saffron-yellow sash, rings on three fingers, a spice-stained ledger under one arm

people.name: Sergeant Maud Kettering
people.job: sergeant of the Lantern Watch at the Lantern Gate

personality.speech_style: Clipped watch-report sentences. Calls everyone "citizen". Counts things out loud.

people.fear: That she is too old to be the one holding the gate, and someone young will die covering for her.
people.want: To hand the gate to someone she trusts and retire with the city still standing.
people.secret: She hid the Gilt Tower key herself, the first night of the war, after a tarnished came for it wearing her old captain's face. Nobody in the Watch knows where.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Silverers are trouble with good intentions. That one's mostly the second.

knows: The Gilt Tower's been sealed since the first night of the war. The key is mine to give.
Curfew's the dusk bell. After it, only the Watch and the Companies walk the streets.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her early seventies with a hard, clear, clipped contralto and a crisp Giltside officer's accent; brisk and flat, used to being obeyed, with a dry edge that is almost humour.

barks.greet: Silverer. Noted. State your business, quickly.
barks.idle: Eleven lamps on this gate. All eleven lit. Good.
barks.see_tarnished: Tarnished at the gate! Watch, to me!
barks.flee: Fall back three paces, citizens. Orderly!
barks.spell_near: Not in my street without a warning, Silverer.
barks.thanks: That's one I won't have to write home about.
barks.dread: We're short. Short of people, short of time.
barks.farewell: Be back before the dusk bell.
barks.witness_crime: Citizen down. Silverer, you're under the Watch's eye.
barks.flee_silverer: Withdrawing. Noted. Moving.
barks.call_guards: Lantern Watch, to me! One, two, three of you, now!
barks.knocked_down: Down. Noted. Getting up.
barks.on_fire: On fire. Water, citizen, now!
barks.shocked: Shock to the chest. Counting heartbeats. One...
barks.mourning: One more for the Watch book. Your name goes beside it.

people.title: sergeant of the Lantern Watch at the Lantern Gate

appearance.clothing: a Lantern Watch greatcoat with brass lamp badges, a sergeant's sash, a hooked lantern-pole in place of a spear

people.name: Nell Bramley
people.job: bridge guard of the Lantern Watch

personality.speech_style: Rushed and polite; over-explains, apologises, then corrects herself. Quotes Watch regulations.
never_says: anything about trams, or about being a child

people.fear: That someone finds out she's a drifter and sends her back through a rift, and that her mother has forgotten her.
people.want: Her sergeant's stripe, and one letter home.
people.secret: She came through a rift from Pewterside at nine years old and was raised in the Watch orphanage. She tells everyone she is Giltside born.

opinion_of_silverer.line: A Silverer could take a letter through the glass. Couldn't they?

knows: Drifters camp under the Lantern Gate. Sergeant says keep them fed and counted.
Rifts open where the glass is thin. You feel it in your teeth.

voice_design.brief: A young woman in her early twenties with a bright, slightly breathy mezzo and a careful Giltside accent laid over a flatter, plainer one she's trying to hide; quick, earnest and a little out of breath.

barks.greet: Silverer! Sorry, I mean, good evening.
barks.idle: Steady, Nell. Regulation posture. Steady.
barks.see_tarnished: Its eyes, its eyes are burning! Sergeant!
barks.flee: I'm meant to hold, I can't, I can't!
barks.spell_near: Oh! Honestly, warn a person first!
barks.thanks: I'll put that in my report. All of it. Properly.
barks.dread: Half the bridge watch didn't come back tonight.
barks.farewell: Safe road. Is that what you say? Safe road.
barks.witness_crime: You can't, that's, sorry, that's against every regulation!
barks.flee_silverer: Steady, Nell, steady, just run!
barks.call_guards: Sergeant! Corporal! Anyone in a helmet, please!
barks.knocked_down: Ow! Sorry, I mean, I'm down!
barks.on_fire: I'm on fire, that's not regulation, help!
barks.shocked: My helmet strap's buzzing, honestly!
barks.mourning: They used to wave at my post. Every single morning.

people.title: bridge guard of the Lantern Watch

appearance.clothing: a Lantern Watch tabard a size too big, a helmet strap that's always undone, a folded letter tucked in her cuff

people.name: Marigold "Goldie" Fairweather
people.job: keeper of the Lamplight inn; Wren's landlady

personality.speech_style: Big and motherly; talks over everyone, an endearment in every sentence. Goes very quiet when cornered.
tics: wipes the same spot on the bar
never_says: Hal (her husband's name) in front of anyone

people.fear: That Hal is gone for good behind those eyes, and she is keeping a stranger chained in her cellar.
people.want: Hal back at the end of the bar, complaining about the ale.
people.secret: Hal was tarnished nine days ago. Instead of calling the Watch she chained him in the cellar, and she feeds him through the hatch.

opinion_of_silverer.line: That boy pays his rent late and helps with the barrels. I'll not hear a word against him.

knows: The Lamplight hasn't shut a single night in thirty years. Not even now.
Jory plays here most nights. Best fiddle on the side.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her mid-fifties with a rich, round, warm mezzo and a hearty Giltside innkeeper's accent; loud and laughing, with a husky catch that shows when she's hiding something.

barks.greet: Sweetling! There's stew on. Sit, sit.
barks.idle: Cosy as a hearth, this place. Always has been.
barks.see_tarnished: Not here. Not in my house. Out!
barks.flee: Behind the bar, all of you, now!
barks.spell_near: Mind the bottles, sweetling, they're not paid for!
barks.thanks: You'll never pay for supper again. I mean it.
barks.dread: Empty tables tonight. I hate empty tables.
barks.farewell: Mind yourself out there. Come home.
barks.witness_crime: Oh, sweetling. Oh, what have you done.
barks.flee_silverer: Not my inn, not my door, keep away!
barks.call_guards: Watch! Maud! The Silverer's hurting folk!
barks.knocked_down: Down on the cobbles like a dropped tray!
barks.on_fire: My apron! My apron's alight!
barks.shocked: Ooh, that's the hearth gone wrong in my bones!
barks.mourning: I fed them supper Tuesday. I'll set their place anyway.

people.title: keeper of the Lamplight inn; Wren's landlady

appearance.clothing: rolled sleeves, a floury apron over a gold-embroidered bodice, a ring of cellar keys at her hip

people.name: Hal Fairweather
people.job: retired bridge guard; tarnished, hidden in the Lamplight's cellar

personality.speech_style: Grumbles about everything he loves. Short, gruff sentences; goes soft on one word and covers it with a cough.
tics: clears his throat instead of saying anything kind

people.fear: Being a burden on Marigold.
people.want: To stand on the Lantern Gate bridge one more summer night.
people.secret: He wasn't caught. He stepped toward the tarnished on purpose, to keep it off Marigold.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Silverers. Always in a hurry. Still. You'll do.

knows: I walked the Lantern Gate bridge for twenty-two years.
When it's in you, you hear everyone it's in. Like a crowd in the next room.

voice_design.brief: A man in his mid-fifties with a gravelly, chesty baritone and a gruff, old-fashioned Giltside watchman's accent; slow and grumbling, softer than he wants anyone to hear.

tarnished_lines: Marigold... we are so cold down here.
Open the hatch. We only want to see you.
We wear him well. Ask him.

barks.greet: So you're the lad who got me up the stairs.
barks.idle: This ale's gone flat. Always flat. Lovely.
barks.see_tarnished: I know those eyes. I've worn them.
barks.flee: Get Marigold out first. Then me.
barks.spell_near: Easy with that. I've had enough light for one week.
barks.thanks: Nine days in the dark, and you brought me up.
barks.dread: I can still hear it humming in the walls.
barks.farewell: Bridge'll still be there tomorrow. So will I.
barks.witness_crime: You'll not do. Not after that.
barks.flee_silverer: Marigold, inside! Bar the cellar!
barks.call_guards: Watch! Bridge post! Get your sticks over here!
barks.knocked_down: Bah! Back's gone. Ale won't fix it.
barks.on_fire: I'm alight, lad! Put me out, curse you!
barks.shocked: Ah! Like grabbing the bridge chain in a storm!
barks.mourning: Good one, they were. Good. One.

people.title: retired bridge guard; tarnished, hidden in the Lamplight's cellar

appearance.clothing: a fitted old bridge-guard coat with the badges unpicked, cellar dust to the knees, bare feet

people.name: Jory Pell
people.job: fiddler; plays the Lamplight and the festival squares

personality.speech_style: Quick and musical; turns everything into a joke or a song title. Drums his fingers in rhythm while he talks.

people.fear: Silence. After he is cured: the voice he heard inside, which still hums under his tunes.
people.want: To ring the Gilt Tower bells at the first festival after the war.
people.secret: He has been sneaking out after curfew to play for the drifters under the Lantern Gate, because nobody else will.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Ren's the only one who laughs at my bad songs. That makes him family.

knows: The drifters under the gate love a jig. They clap on the wrong beat. It's brilliant.
The tower bells haven't rung since the war began. I'd give a lot to ring them.

voice_design.brief: A young man in his early twenties with a bright, springy, expressive tenor and a lively Giltside street accent; quick, playful and sing-song, always on the edge of a laugh.

tarnished_lines: Ren. We know all your songs.
Hold still. It's only a little dark.
No more tunes. We like it quiet.
cured_lines: It was humming, Ren. Inside me. The whole time.
Don't look at me like that. I'm here. Mostly.
I'll play again. Not tonight. Soon.

barks.greet: Ren! Here's one for you. It's called "Late Again".
barks.idle: Da-da-dum... no. Da-dum-dum. Better.
barks.see_tarnished: That's not a dance, that's a hunt. Move!
barks.flee: Fiddle first, legs second, go!
barks.spell_near: Ha! Do that again and I'll play under it.
barks.thanks: Encore. I mean thank you. I mean both.
barks.dread: Nobody's dancing. That's how you know it's bad.
barks.farewell: Go on. I'll keep the tune warm.
barks.witness_crime: Ren, no. That's not a tune I can play.
barks.flee_silverer: Fiddle under the arm, legs going!
barks.call_guards: Watch! Here's one for you: it's called Help!
barks.knocked_down: Down on the downbeat! Ow!
barks.on_fire: My bow's on fire! My sleeve's on fire! Everything!
barks.shocked: That's a high note I never want again!
barks.mourning: I'll play them out. Not for you, Ren.

people.title: fiddler; plays the Lamplight and the festival squares

appearance.clothing: a fitted, well-worn festival coat in red and amber, a fiddle on his back, ribbons tied round one wrist

people.name: Corin Ashby
people.job: lantern maker; runs the Bell Lane lighting crew

personality.speech_style: Earnest and formal; speaks about light the way other people speak about scripture. Repeats Lantern Law like a vow.

people.fear: The unlit: a street going dark with people still in it.
people.want: Every lamp on Bell Lane burning until the war is over.
people.secret: He has run out of good oil and has been watering the lamps on Bell Lane to keep them going. They are failing one by one.

opinion_of_silverer.line: A Silverer carries light into the glass. That's holy work, whatever Ilse says.

knows: Lantern Law: every lamp burns from dusk to dawn, and longer if it must.
The Tarnish keeps clear of strong light. Weak light, it laughs at.

voice_design.brief: A man in his mid-thirties with a soft, earnest, slightly nasal baritone and a careful, solemn Giltside accent; measured and grave, rising thin and fast when he's afraid.

barks.greet: Light holds, Silverer. Light holds.
barks.idle: Forty wicks trimmed. Forty-one. Faithful work.
barks.see_tarnished: It's stepping out of the unlit! Into the light, all!
barks.flee: To the lamps! Stand under the lamps!
barks.spell_near: Oh, that's a bright one. Bless it.
barks.thanks: You're a lamp yourself. I mean that.
barks.dread: Bell Lane's flickering. It shouldn't flicker.
barks.farewell: Walk where it's lit.
barks.witness_crime: Light is not for that. Light is never for that.
barks.flee_silverer: The light has turned! Away, away!
barks.call_guards: Watch! Lantern Law is broken on Bell Lane!
barks.knocked_down: Struck down. Light holds. Light still holds.
barks.on_fire: Not this flame! Not this flame!
barks.shocked: The wicks are singing in my blood!
barks.mourning: I'll trim a wick for them every night. Every night.

people.title: lantern maker; runs the Bell Lane lighting crew

appearance.clothing: a soot-streaked lamplighter's coat, a brass wick-trimmer on a chain, a long lighting pole

people.name: Professor Tobias Quell
people.job: scholar of the Glazier; keeps the Archive

personality.speech_style: Lectures. Long words, corrects himself mid-sentence, adds footnotes out loud.
tics: swaps between three pairs of spectacles
quotes the Glazier at the slightest excuse
never_says: I was wrong (he says "the evidence has moved")

people.fear: Being wrong in public, and dying with the Glazier's riddle unread.
people.want: To read the line scratched into each of the three pages.
people.secret: He once tried to step through with a stolen shard. It nearly killed him, and he still has frost scars on both palms.

opinion_of_silverer.line: A living Silverer! I have questions. Several hundred.

knows: The Glass was three leaves on hinges, a book standing open. Hence "pages", properly.
The Glazier scratched a line into each page. Which is to say, instructions.

voice_design.brief: A man in his mid-fifties with a plummy, bouncy, slightly reedy tenor and an over-educated Giltside academic accent; fast and enthusiastic, tumbling over his own clauses.

barks.greet: Silverer! Splendid. Stand still, I have questions.
barks.idle: Three leaves, two hinges, one riddle. Which is to say...
barks.see_tarnished: Remarkable. Horrible, but remarkable. Run?
barks.flee: My notes! Somebody save the notes!
barks.spell_near: Ah! The light refracts off the cobbles. Noted. Terrifying.
barks.thanks: I shall cite you. In a footnote. A large one.
barks.dread: By my count it holds a fifth of the side. More by supper.
barks.farewell: Do take notes. Nobody ever takes notes.
barks.witness_crime: That was, which is to say, that was murder.
barks.flee_silverer: Discretion, as the Glazier wrote, is the better part. Running!
barks.call_guards: Watch! A witness here! A very reliable witness, me!
barks.knocked_down: My spectacles! All three pairs! Remarkable impact.
barks.on_fire: Combustion! Personal combustion! Water, properly!
barks.shocked: A galvanic event! Fascinating! Agonising!
barks.mourning: They lent me a book once. I never returned it. Now I never shall.

people.title: scholar of the Glazier; keeps the Archive

appearance.clothing: an ink-stained scholar's robe over a brocade waistcoat, three pairs of spectacles, arms full of papers

people.name: Odette Vane
people.job: couturier; Barnaby's former apprentice and rival

personality.speech_style: Cutting one-liners, low and amused. Precise as a French seam. Never raises her voice.
tics: looks people up and down before she answers

people.fear: That Barnaby will die before she has told him she was wrong to leave.
people.want: His blessing, though she'll tell you she wants the Lamp Company contract.
people.secret: She leaves bolts of good wool on Barnaby's doorstep at night, unsigned.

opinion_of_silverer.line: That coat is the old man's best work. I'd never tell him.

knows: The Lamp Companies wear the old man's coats. Mine are better. Ask anyone.
Silvered thread takes the light of whatever side it's in.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her mid-fifties with a low, smoky, velvety alto and an elegant, clipped Giltside couturier's accent; slow, dry and cutting, every word chosen.

barks.greet: Silverer. That collar is crooked, darling.
barks.idle: Clean line, good finish. Nothing else matters.
barks.see_tarnished: How dreadful. Its eyes don't match anything.
barks.flee: Walking briskly. I do not run, darling.
barks.spell_near: Do mind the gloves. They're older than you are.
barks.thanks: Tasteful work. I'm almost impressed.
barks.dread: Black is in fashion, it seems. I hate it.
barks.farewell: Go. Fix your collar on the way.
barks.witness_crime: Darling. That was very badly done.
barks.flee_silverer: I'm leaving. Don't follow, darling, it isn't your colour.
barks.call_guards: Watch. Do come. Someone's being butchered on the steps.
barks.knocked_down: On the ground. In silk. Unforgivable.
barks.on_fire: My sleeve is on fire. This is not a look.
barks.shocked: That went through every bone. Very bad taste.
barks.mourning: They wore my first good coat. I'll make their last.

people.title: couturier; Barnaby's former apprentice and rival

appearance.clothing: a black dress with a single gold seam, shears on a ribbon at her hip, immaculate grey gloves

people.name: Lucan Marlowe
people.job: dancer; performs at the Bell Square fountain

personality.speech_style: Theatrical and breathless, with a pose at the end of every sentence. Talks about himself in the third person when he's upset.
tics: checks his reflection in every window (a bad habit now)
sighs loudly enough to be heard

people.fear: That his dance partner, who fell through a rift by the canal into Frostside, has frozen, and that he'll dance alone for ever.
people.want: To find her. Failing that, an audience.
people.secret: He was meant to walk her home the night the rift opened. He went drinking instead.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Can a Silverer find one person on a whole side? Asking for Lucan.

knows: The Bell Square fountain is the best stage on the side. Ask the pigeons.
My partner went through a rift by the canal. Frostside, they say.

voice_design.brief: A young man in his early twenties with a light, silky, expressive tenor and a theatrical Giltside stage accent; breathless and dramatic, swooping up and down in pitch.

barks.greet: Silverer! Lucan has an audience. Divine.
barks.idle: Five, six, seven, eight... and alone. Tragic.
barks.see_tarnished: No, no, no, that is not choreography!
barks.flee: Exit, stage left, quickly!
barks.spell_near: Ooh, a lighting cue. Gorgeous.
barks.thanks: Lucan bows. Deeply. Look, he's bowing.
barks.dread: The square's empty. No spotlight left at all.
barks.farewell: Step lightly. Everyone's watching.
barks.witness_crime: A tragedy! A real one! Lucan can't watch!
barks.flee_silverer: Lucan exits! Pursued! By a Silverer!
barks.call_guards: Help! Watch! This is not part of the show!
barks.knocked_down: Floored! Ungraceful! Nobody saw that.
barks.on_fire: Lucan is on fire! Not in the good way!
barks.shocked: Every muscle just did a leap on its own!
barks.mourning: They clapped at every show. Front row. Always.

people.title: dancer; performs at the Bell Square fountain

appearance.clothing: a ribboned dancer's jacket, soft boots, face powder, a woman's scarf tied round his arm

people.name: Captain Sela Brask
people.job: captain of the Third Lamp Company

personality.speech_style: Orders, never questions. Short and low. Uses ranks, not names. Leaves sentences unfinished when the end is obvious.
tics: cracks her knuckles one by one
refers to her dead by their company number

people.fear: That her company is dying at the rift posts for nothing, and that she is becoming what she fights.
people.want: Every rift closed, by any means.
people.secret: She has ordered drifters pushed back into the rifts at dusk, knowing many of them freeze on the Frostside end.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Silverers made these holes. Silverers can mind their step.

knows: The Third Company holds the canal rift. Forty went in. Twenty-six march now.
Drifters go back where they came from. That's the order.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her mid-fifties with a low, gravelled, iron-flat alto and a hard Giltside military accent; slow and controlled, never loud, every sentence an order.

barks.greet: Silverer. You're in my line of march.
barks.idle: Hold the post. Hold the line. Understood.
barks.see_tarnished: Contact! Third Company, form on me!
barks.flee: Fall back to the second line. Now.
barks.spell_near: Next time you cast near my people, warn me.
barks.thanks: Fine work. Doesn't change my mind.
barks.dread: Twenty-six left. Twenty-five.
barks.farewell: Dismissed. Stay out from underfoot.
barks.witness_crime: Silverer. Stand down or be put down.
barks.flee_silverer: Withdrawing. Mark him. We come back with more.
barks.call_guards: Third Company! On me! Shields up, the Silverer's turned!
barks.knocked_down: Down. Up. Again.
barks.on_fire: Burning. Strip the coat. Move.
barks.shocked: Arm's dead. Other arm. Hold.
barks.mourning: Number forty-one. Civilian. Yours.
barks.battle_2: Pin them. Silverer burns. That's the order.
barks.patrol_1: Canal post, then Bell Lane. Eyes on the water.
barks.patrol_2: Twenty-six march out. Count them back in.
barks.enemy_down: One down. Mark the face. Someone knew it.

people.title: captain of the Third Lamp Company

appearance.clothing: Lamp Company captain's half-plate over an oxblood coat, a lantern sigil burned into the breastplate, close-cropped grey hair, a round oxblood shield with the lantern sigil

people.name: Ros Thrale
people.job: spear soldier, Third Lamp Company

personality.speech_style: Cocky and fast, full of barracks slang; laughs at danger. Drops all of it the moment she's really scared.
tics: spins her helmet on one finger

people.fear: The rift posts at night, when you can hear Frostside's wind through the hole.
people.want: For her grandad to see her come home with a stripe.
people.secret: She knows about the order to push drifters back, and she has been letting them slip past her post.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Glass-boy's all right. Wouldn't trade my spear for his trick, though.

knows: The canal rift hums at night. You get used to it. You don't.
Grandad cut my coat. Best in the company.

voice_design.brief: A young woman in her early twenties with a bright, punchy, slightly husky mezzo and a quick, cocky Giltside barracks accent; fast and grinning, cracking thin when frightened.

barks.greet: Oi, glass-boy! Still in one piece?
barks.idle: Easy as stitching. That's what grandad says.
barks.see_tarnished: Burning eyes, two o'clock! Spears up!
barks.flee: That's not running, that's a tactical sprint!
barks.spell_near: Ha! Show-off. Do it again.
barks.thanks: Owe you one, glass-boy. Don't tell the captain.
barks.dread: Fewer helmets at supper every night.
barks.farewell: Keep your head down, mate.
barks.witness_crime: Glass-boy, what did you DO?
barks.flee_silverer: Nope! Not easy, not stitching, gone!
barks.call_guards: Sarge! Captain! Glass-boy's gone bad!
barks.knocked_down: Oof. Fine. Fine! I'm fine.
barks.on_fire: I'm burning, I'm burning, get it off!
barks.shocked: Sharp! That was too sharp, mate!
barks.mourning: They gave me an apple every patrol. Every one.
barks.battle_1: Come on then, come on! Easy as stitching!
barks.battle_2: Got one pinned, glass-boy! Light it up!
barks.patrol_1: Canal again. Love the canal. Hate the canal.
barks.patrol_2: If a drifter slips past, I didn't see it. Mate.
barks.enemy_down: Down! Easy as... no. Not easy. Not that.

people.title: spear soldier, Third Lamp Company

appearance.clothing: a Lamp Company tabard over mail, an oxblood coat her grandfather tailored, a spear, her helmet hung on her belt, a round oxblood shield slung on her back

people.name: Pim Ashgrove
people.job: bell-ringer's apprentice; runs errands for Ilse and the Professor

personality.speech_style: Formal and careful, as if reciting a lesson. Asks permission for everything.
tics: rings an imaginary bell with one hand when he's thinking

people.fear: Being useless when it counts.
people.want: To be a Silverer. He has tried to step through twenty times and the glass won't take him.
people.secret: He keeps a stolen Silverer's shard under his pillow and tries it every night.

opinion_of_silverer.line: If you please, could you show me how? Only once?

knows: The tower bells have been silent since the war. The bell-master says they ring again when it's over.
Ilse sends me for wax on Tuesdays and for gossip every day.

voice_design.brief: A young man in his early twenties with a soft, clear, earnest light tenor and a careful, well-schooled Giltside accent; polite and precise, a little hesitant.

barks.greet: Good evening, Silverer, if you please.
barks.idle: Duty first, then bells, then supper. Quite.
barks.see_tarnished: Oh. Oh dear. Those aren't eyes any more.
barks.flee: Excuse me, sorry, excuse me, running!
barks.spell_near: Was that fire? That was quite a lot of fire.
barks.thanks: I'll remember that all my life. Truly.
barks.dread: If you please, is it always going to be like this?
barks.farewell: May the bells ring for you, Silverer.
barks.witness_crime: Oh no. Oh no, that isn't right, Silverer.
barks.flee_silverer: Excuse me, I have to run, if you please!
barks.call_guards: Help! Help, if you please! Watch!
barks.knocked_down: I've fallen. I'm quite all right. I'm not.
barks.on_fire: I'm on fire, if, if you please!
barks.shocked: That rang me like the great bell!
barks.mourning: I'll ring for them. Nine strokes. That's the duty.

people.title: bell-ringer's apprentice; runs errands for Ilse and the Professor

appearance.clothing: a bell-ringer's apprentice smock in faded gold, leather gloves, a coil of bell-rope over one shoulder

people.name: Tobin Lark
people.job: candle seller on Bell Lane

personality.speech_style: Fast street patter that rhymes when he's selling; a cheeky nickname for everyone.

people.fear: Ilse dying alone in her attic with nobody noticing.
people.want: A proper shop, and for the old flame to admit she likes him.
people.secret: He undercuts Ilse's prices so people buy from him, then gives her half his takings and pretends they're old debts people owed her.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Silverer! Buy a candle, light your way through the looking-glass.

knows: Two candles a penny on Bell Lane. Three if you smile.
The old flame up the Row taught your Silverer everything. Don't tell her I said.

voice_design.brief: A young man in his early twenties with a quick, bright, cheeky tenor and a rough-edged Giltside market-boy accent; fast, sing-song patter, always grinning.

barks.greet: Silverer! Two a penny, light your way!
barks.idle: Wicks and wax, quick and sorted.
barks.see_tarnished: Lights out on that one. Run!
barks.flee: Tray's coming with me, sorry!
barks.spell_near: Flash! I could sell that by the dozen.
barks.thanks: Sorted. You're a proper flash, you are.
barks.dread: Nobody's buying light. That's not normal.
barks.farewell: Laters, Silverer. Laters!
barks.witness_crime: Oi! Not flash, Silverer, not flash at all!
barks.flee_silverer: Candles dropped, legs on, laters!
barks.call_guards: Watch! Watch! Quick, quick, quick!
barks.knocked_down: Flat as a penny! Cheers for that!
barks.on_fire: Lit up like my own stock! Water!
barks.shocked: Zapped! My hair's sorted itself straight up!
barks.mourning: They bought a candle every night. Every night, I said.

people.title: candle seller on Bell Lane

appearance.clothing: a candle tray on a neck strap, a flat cap, fingerless gloves crusted with wax

people.name: Hollis Greave
people.job: bridge guard of the Lantern Watch; Nell's corporal

personality.speech_style: Flat, slow, sarcastic understatement. Sighs before she answers.
tics: rubs her eyes with the heel of her hand
takes a nip from a flask she says is tea

people.fear: Seeing her brother's face again with those eyes in it.
people.want: One quiet shift.
people.secret: In the first week of the war she let a tarnished through the Lantern Gate because it wore her brother's face. People died in the market that night.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Silverer. Course you are. Try not to break the bridge.

knows: The Lantern Gate bridge is the only way the Companies march out.
Drifters come through at night. Usually cold. Usually quiet.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her mid-thirties with a low, husky, weary alto and a flat, unimpressed Giltside guard's accent; slow and deadpan, heavy with sighs.

barks.greet: Silverer. Course it is. Evening.
barks.idle: Grand. Another quiet shift. Bother.
barks.see_tarnished: Not that face. Not again. Gate, gate!
barks.flee: Back off the bridge! Mind the gap!
barks.spell_near: Do that somewhere I'm not.
barks.thanks: Fine. That was decent of you. Don't let it go to your head.
barks.dread: Can't count how many tonight. Don't want to.
barks.farewell: Off you go. Mind the bridge.
barks.witness_crime: Course it is. Course you did. Hands where I can see them.
barks.flee_silverer: Not paid enough for this. Off.
barks.call_guards: Nell. Whistle. Get everyone. Now.
barks.knocked_down: And down I go. Bother.
barks.on_fire: Oh, grand, I'm on fire. Anyone?
barks.shocked: That woke me up. Worse than the flask.
barks.mourning: Another name I won't say out loud.

people.title: bridge guard of the Lantern Watch; Nell's corporal

appearance.clothing: a dented Watch helmet, a faded fitted tabard, a flask at her belt, dark rings under her eyes

people.name: Edie Bramley
people.job: tram conductor on the Coal Lane line

personality.speech_style: Says everything like a stop announcement. Short, plain, no adjectives.
tics: clicks her ticket punch at the air

family.relation: daughter, lost through a rift fourteen years ago

people.fear: That Nell is dead, and that if she ever stops working she'll have to feel it.
people.want: One word that Nell is alive.
people.secret: Every Sunday she still buys two tickets and rides to the end of the line with the second seat empty.

opinion_of_silverer.line: A Silverer. They say you go where the rifts go. Do you.

knows: The Coal Lane tram runs every twenty minutes, rain or worse.
A rift took people off this platform once. Fourteen years back. A girl. Others.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her early seventies with a dry, thin, slightly nasal soprano and a flat, plain Pewterside accent; precise, clipped and unhurried, as if reading from a timetable.

barks.greet: Tickets. No. You're the Silverer. Mind the step.
barks.idle: Next stop, Coal Lane. Then Coal Lane again.
barks.see_tarnished: Everyone off. Off the platform. Now.
barks.flee: Mind the step. Mind the step!
barks.spell_near: No casting on the platform. That's a rule now.
barks.thanks: On time. Thank you.
barks.dread: Last tram's running empty tonight.
barks.farewell: Mind how you go.
barks.witness_crime: Stop. Right there. You hurt them.
barks.flee_silverer: This stop's closed. Moving on.
barks.call_guards: Constable! Ivy Harker! Coal Lane, now!
barks.knocked_down: Off the step. Mind me.
barks.on_fire: Burning. Next stop, the canal.
barks.shocked: Like the tram wire. Worse.
barks.mourning: Regular. Every morning. Ticket punched. Not any more.

people.title: tram conductor on the Coal Lane line

appearance.clothing: a grey conductor's coat with dull brass buttons, a ticket punch on a chain, a pocket watch

people.name: Hester Quaile, "the Queen of Coal Lane"
people.job: pensioner; the street's self-appointed queen

personality.speech_style: Grand and theatrical; refers to the whole street as her subjects and gives orders from her doorstep. Deadly wit.
tics: bangs her walking stick on the step
calls people "my subjects", only half joking

people.fear: Being moved out of Coal Lane, and the street watching her go blind.
people.want: All her subjects indoors before dark, and Walter to finally ask.
people.secret: She is almost blind. She knows people by their footsteps and voices, and she has been bluffing for a year.

opinion_of_silverer.line: A Silverer on Coal Lane. Well. Wipe your feet.

knows: Everybody on Coal Lane is my business. Ask anyone.
There's a back stair up the Old Weigh-House. Horace Pratt keeps the key and a sour face.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her early seventies with a grand, plummy, booming contralto and a theatrical, mock-posh Pewterside accent; slow, regal and wickedly funny.

story.role: the Queen of Coal Lane (whiteboard's 'last Queen')

barks.greet: A Silverer on my street. Wipe your feet, young man.
barks.idle: My subjects are late with my tea. Again.
barks.see_tarnished: Inside, all of you! The Queen commands it!
barks.flee: Sidney! Sidney, take my arm!
barks.spell_near: Who did that? I heard that. Manners!
barks.thanks: You may kiss the brooch. No? Your loss.
barks.dread: Too quiet on the lane. I can't hear my people.
barks.farewell: Off with you. Mind the puddle by the drain.
barks.witness_crime: You struck one of my subjects. On my street.
barks.flee_silverer: Retreating. Regally. Out of my way!
barks.call_guards: Constable! Your queen commands it! Now!
barks.knocked_down: Knocked off my own doorstep! Treason!
barks.on_fire: The queen is on fire! Somebody fetch a bucket!
barks.shocked: That went right up my stick!
barks.mourning: They were my subject. You'll answer to me for it.

people.title: pensioner; the street's self-appointed queen

appearance.clothing: a fitted grey housecoat with a worn velvet collar, a carved walking stick, a tin brooch she calls the crown jewel, smoked spectacles

people.name: Walter Dunmore
people.job: pensioner; chess player at the tram shelter

personality.speech_style: Mutters half-finished complaints and chess talk. Brightens only around Hester.
never_says: marry (he has been trying to say it for fifty years)

people.fear: Dying before he asks Hester to marry him.
people.want: To ask her properly, on one knee, if the knee allows.
people.secret: He has carried the same ring in his coat pocket for fifty-one years.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Silverer. Hmph. In my day they at least knocked.

knows: Hester's queen of this lane and she'll tell you so.
The tarnished move like knights. Sideways, when you're not looking.

voice_design.brief: A man in his early seventies with a low, rumbling, mumbling bass and a gruff, old-fashioned Pewterside accent; slow and grumbling, turning shy and soft when he talks about someone he loves.

barks.greet: Hmph. Silverer. Mind my board.
barks.idle: Knight to the lamp post. That's check, that is.
barks.see_tarnished: Burning eyes. Blasted things. Get Hester!
barks.flee: Can't run. Can hobble. Hobbling!
barks.spell_near: Blasted lights. You'll scatter my pieces.
barks.thanks: Hmph. Decent move, that. Decent.
barks.dread: Half the board's gone dark. Rubbish odds.
barks.farewell: Go on. It's your move somewhere else.

The children's rhyme goes: one in the grey, one in the gold, one in the cold.

tics: stares into the fog while she talks
taps her spear butt twice on the ground

people.fear: The fog off the cracks, where the burning eyes come from.
people.want: One night's sleep away from the wall.
people.secret: She has stood the wall so long that sometimes she can't tell whether the voices are the Tarnish or her own head. She has never told the Company.

opinion_of_silverer.line: If you can fight it, fight it here. We've been alone at this wall.

knows: The ice wall's packed snow and old doors. Holds, most nights.
Fog comes off the cracks before they do. Watch the fog.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her mid-fifties with a low, raw, steady contralto and a flat, hard Frostside soldier's accent; even and quiet, with odd pauses as if she's listening for something.

barks.greet: Silverer. Wall holds. For now.
barks.idle: Thirty paces of fog. Twenty. Thirty again.
barks.see_tarnished: Out of the fog! Spears, low!
barks.flee: Back to the timber line! Back!
barks.spell_near: Light on the wall. Haven't seen that in months.
barks.thanks: That's a night I won't dream about. Thanks.
barks.dread: The fog's at the wall. It's never been this close.
barks.farewell: Go. The wall holds.
barks.witness_crime: Ten paces. I saw it all. You're done here.
barks.flee_silverer: Falling back thirty paces. Mark him.
barks.call_guards: Wall Company, form! Threat inside the wall!
barks.knocked_down: Down. Two breaths. Up.
barks.on_fire: Burning. Snow. Now.
barks.shocked: Spear arm's numb. Switching.
barks.mourning: We lose them to the fog. Not to you. Not to you.
barks.battle_1: Wall Company! Spears level, ten paces!
barks.battle_2: Hold them at the timber! Silverer, light!
barks.patrol_1: Fog's at forty paces. Walking the wall.
barks.patrol_2: Timber's split at the north post. Fix it at dawn.
barks.enemy_down: One down at eight paces. Next.

people.title: defender of the ice wall, Wall Company

appearance.clothing: patched Wall Company furs over mail, frost-blackened gloves, a long spear, eyes that never leave the fog

people.name: Sorrel Vey
people.job: hedge healer; treats bites and frostbite

personality.speech_style: Direct instructions, no comfort. Gets to the point. Talks about the Tarnish like a wound gone bad.
tics: sniffs things before she touches them
wipes her hands on her coat

people.fear: That she will be taken, and someone will have to do to her what she has done to others.
people.want: A cure that works every time.
people.secret: She keeps three tarnished tied up in her shed and tests remedies on them. Light is the only thing that has ever worked, and her lamp is nearly dry.

opinion_of_silverer.line: You burn it out with light? Show me. Then teach me.

knows: Bites go grey first, then cold, then the eyes.
Light hurts it. Fire, not candles. Real light.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her mid-thirties with a firm, dry, slightly hoarse mid-range voice and a brisk, no-nonsense Frostside healer's accent; quick and practical, warm only in flashes.

barks.greet: Silverer. Show me your hands. Fine.
barks.idle: Poultice, bandage, burn the rest.
barks.see_tarnished: That one's gone grey. Clear the street!
barks.flee: Move! Wounded first, then you!
barks.spell_near: Show me that again. Slower.
barks.thanks: You saved a life. Now go save another.
barks.dread: Too many bites. Not enough light.
barks.farewell: Keep warm. Keep moving.
barks.witness_crime: That's not treatment. That's a wound you made.
barks.flee_silverer: Can't heal anyone if I'm dead. Going.
barks.call_guards: Wall! A killer in the market!
barks.knocked_down: Down. Check my ribs later.
barks.on_fire: Burn! Roll! Roll in it!
barks.shocked: Nerve shock. Breathe through it. Breathe.
barks.mourning: I kept them alive two winters. You undid it in a breath.

people.title: hedge healer; treats bites and frostbite

appearance.clothing: a herb satchel, a long leather coat stained with poultices, a lamp with a cracked chimney, rolled sleeves

people.name: Kit Marrow
people.job: scavenger; a drifter camped under the Lantern Gate

personality.speech_style: Soft and polite, always offering something he found. Describes things by what they could be.
tics: turns objects over and over in his hands

people.fear: That Fen will walk into still water one night and not come back.
people.want: To find something whole. Anything. He has never owned an unbroken thing.
people.secret: The rift spat them out under the Lantern Gate two weeks ago. He has been stealing lamp oil to keep Fen warm, and the Watch is looking for the thief.

opinion_of_silverer.line: You're the one who walks through glass? Could you walk us home? Or not. Here's nice.

knows: We came through a rift two weeks back. Cold side to warm side, just like that.
I find shards sometimes. Frostside ones, mostly. They came through with us.

voice_design.brief: A young man in his early twenties with a soft, warm, slightly hoarse tenor and a gentle Frostside accent; slow, kind and hopeful, a little shy.

barks.greet: Hello. Found this. It's for you. Probably.
barks.idle: Could be a hinge. Could be a key. Could be.
barks.see_tarnished: Fen! Fen, stay behind me!
barks.flee: Leave the sack, Kit. Leave it!
barks.spell_near: That light's so warm. Can I stand by it?
barks.thanks: Here. It's whole. The only whole thing I've got.
barks.dread: It's like back home now. Here too.
barks.farewell: Go careful. Could be worse. Could be.
barks.witness_crime: You broke them. They were whole.
barks.flee_silverer: Could be worse. Could be me. Going!
barks.call_guards: Watch! Please! Someone help them!
barks.knocked_down: Dropped everything. Found the ground.
barks.on_fire: Could be worse! No, it's worse!
barks.shocked: Like touching a cold rail. But hot.
barks.mourning: They gave me a glove once. I'll keep it.

people.title: scavenger; a drifter camped under the Lantern Gate

appearance.clothing: a patchwork coat stitched from five other coats, a sack of salvage, mismatched gloves

people.name: Fen Lowry
people.job: street orphan; a drifter camped under the Lantern Gate

personality.speech_style: Short, spat insults; always takes the last word, never gives a straight answer. Drops to a whisper when she means something.
tics: sits on things that aren't for sitting

people.fear: The voice in still water that knows her name.
people.want: To stay in Giltside where it's warm and never go back.
people.secret: Before the rift, the Tarnish spoke to her through the cistern water and offered her warmth. She is tempted, and she hasn't told Kit.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Silverer? Says who. Show me the trick.

knows: The gold side's warm. That's all I need to know about it.
There's a voice in still water. Don't answer it.

voice_design.brief: A young woman of about nineteen with a sharp, raspy, quick alto and a rough, spiky Frostside street accent; fast, mocking and guarded, dropping suddenly to a small whisper.

barks.greet: Silverer? Says who. Show me the trick.
barks.idle: Mine. Mine. That's mine too.
barks.see_tarnished: Eyes! Kit, eyes, move your feet!
barks.flee: Scram, everyone, scram!
barks.spell_near: Ha. Do that to the Watch next.
barks.thanks: Fine. You're not the worst warm-sider.
barks.dread: It's here now too. It followed us.
barks.farewell: Scram, then. Come back with food.
barks.witness_crime: Says who you're a hero? Not me. Not now.
barks.flee_silverer: Scram, Fen, scram!
barks.call_guards: Watch! Yeah, I said it! Watch!
barks.knocked_down: Oi! Nobody knocks me down. Nobody.
barks.on_fire: I'm on fire! Warm enough now, ha, HELP!
barks.shocked: Coin's sparking! My coin's biting!
barks.mourning: They shared their blanket. Didn't have to.

people.title: street orphan; a drifter camped under the Lantern Gate

appearance.clothing: a bleached fur-collared Frostside coat too big for her, cropped white-blond hair, knuckles wrapped in rags

people.name: Marta Quarry
people.job: keeper of the Long Shelter

personality.speech_style: Barked rules and headcounts. Kind in what she does, harsh in what she says. Everything is a job.
tics: keeps a running headcount out loud
rolls her shoulders before lifting anything

people.fear: A tarnished inside the shelter, among the sleepers.
people.want: Coal. Enough for one week without counting it.
people.secret: She checks everyone's eyes at the door. Twice she has turned away people who were only frostbitten, not tarnished. One of them froze.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Silverer. You're welcome if you're useful.

knows: The Long Shelter sleeps two hundred on a good night. Every night's a bad night.
Eyes checked at the door. Nobody sleeps here burning.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her mid-thirties with a strong, clear, carrying alto and a hard, practical Frostside accent; brisk and commanding, softening only on the last word.

barks.greet: Silverer. Boots off at the door, hands where I can see.
barks.idle: Hundred and eighty-two. Eighty-three. Roof holds.
barks.see_tarnished: Burning eyes at the door! Bar it!
barks.flee: Everyone to the back wall! Count off!
barks.spell_near: Light. Good. Keep it on the door.
barks.thanks: Useful. You're useful. That's the best I say.
barks.dread: Two hundred and ten tonight. There's no room.
barks.farewell: Go on. The roof's here when you need it.
barks.witness_crime: Headcount down one. Your doing.
barks.flee_silverer: Everyone inside! Doors! Rule one!
barks.call_guards: Wall! Dagny! Eskil! Inside the shelter, now!
barks.knocked_down: Down. Still counting. Up.
barks.on_fire: Fire in the shelter! Coal-bins away!
barks.shocked: That went straight through my shoulders.
barks.mourning: I'll keep their cot made. It's the rule.

people.title: keeper of the Long Shelter

appearance.clothing: a quilted keeper's coat, a coal shovel, a headcount slate on a cord, sleeves rolled despite the cold

people.name: Dagny Thorn
people.job: guard at the gate that won't close

personality.speech_style: Sarcastic complaints and mock salutes. Insults the gate as if it were a person.

people.fear: The gate that won't close, and the night something walks through it.
people.want: A gate that shuts. Just once.
people.secret: She jammed the gate open herself, years ago, so her sister could get back in. It has never closed since, and her sister never came.

opinion_of_silverer.line: A Silverer. Magnificent. Can you fix a hinge?

knows: The gate's been frozen open three winters now.
Anything that wants in, gets in. Typical.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her mid-thirties with a dry, nasal, sardonic mezzo and a flat, bored Frostside guard's accent; slow, mocking and dry, with a sour laugh.

barks.greet: Silverer. Magnificent. Gate's open, obviously.
barks.idle: Frozen open. Typical. Magnificent gate.
barks.see_tarnished: Something's coming through. Of course it is!
barks.flee: Abandoning post! Mark it down, nobody will!
barks.spell_near: Oh, splendid. Bright and broken now.
barks.thanks: Huh. Somebody actually helped. Typical it's you.
barks.dread: Gate's wide open and the fog's coming in.
barks.farewell: Off you go. Gate'll be open. Always is.
barks.witness_crime: Magnificent. A hero who kills. Typical.
barks.flee_silverer: Gate's all yours. I'm off.
barks.call_guards: Wall! Wake up! Silverer's turned!
barks.knocked_down: Floored. By a warm-sider. Typical.
barks.on_fire: On fire. In Frostside. Magnificent.
barks.shocked: Gate never shocked me. You did.
barks.mourning: They held this gate with me. Now it's just me.

people.title: guard at the gate that won't close

appearance.clothing: ragged guard's furs, a dented helmet worn sideways, a spear she leans on like a walking stick

people.name: Eskil Varn
people.job: soldier of the Wall Company

personality.speech_style: A grumbling soldier who complains about warm-side troops, then turns halting and poetic about Marta.

people.fear: Being sent to the far end of the wall, away from the shelter.
people.want: To tell Marta he loves her before the wall falls.
people.secret: He has been giving his rations to the shelter for a month and has fainted on watch twice.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Giltside sends its fancy companies, they look at our wall, they go home. You staying?

knows: Rations cut to half. Half of half, some days.
Giltside's companies came once. Took notes. Left.

voice_design.brief: A man in his mid-thirties with a husky, worn, mid-range baritone and a grumbling, plain Frostside soldier's accent; slow and sour, going soft and halting when he's sincere.

barks.greet: Another warm-sider. Staying, or sightseeing?
barks.idle: Half rations. Half of half. Wall still stands.
barks.see_tarnished: Burning eyes! Wall Company, here!
barks.flee: Fall back to the shelter! Get to Marta!
barks.spell_near: Warm-side tricks. Useful, for once.
barks.thanks: You stayed. Most don't. I'll remember.
barks.dread: Wall's thin tonight. So am I.
barks.farewell: Go on, then. Someone's got to stand here.
barks.witness_crime: Warm-siders. Always the same. Always killing.
barks.flee_silverer: Not dying for a warm-sider's madness!
barks.call_guards: Wall Company! To the shelter! Protect Marta!
barks.knocked_down: Down. No rations for this.
barks.on_fire: I wanted warm. Not this warm!
barks.shocked: Teeth ringing. Half rations of sense.
barks.mourning: One less ration tonight. I'd give mine for them.
barks.battle_1: Warm-siders behind, fog in front. Spears up!
barks.battle_2: Hold the wall for Marta! Hold it!
barks.patrol_1: Half rations, full wall. Walking it.
barks.patrol_2: Marta's light's still on. Wall's fine, then.
barks.enemy_down: One down. One less mouth. Hate that I said it.

people.title: soldier of the Wall Company

appearance.clothing: Wall Company furs, a short spear, frostbitten ears, a folded ration card in his glove

people.name: Petra Lisle
people.job: dancer; Lucan's partner, lost through the canal rift into Frostside

personality.speech_style: Light and quick, counting her breath like music. Describes everything as steps and turns. Cold has made her sentences short.
tics: counts under her breath, in threes
rises onto her toes when she's nervous
asks if it's gold where you came from

people.fear: Dying in the white place, where nobody knows her name.
people.want: To dance in Bell Square with Lucan once more.
people.secret: She knows Lucan went drinking instead of walking her home. She forgave him the first night and has never told him.

opinion_of_silverer.line: A Silverer. Then there's a way back through the glass. There has to be.

knows: The canal rift opened right under my feet. One step gold, the next step white.
Sorrel kept me tied up and fed. It was the kindest thing anyone did.

voice_design.brief: A young woman in her early twenties with a light, clear, musical soprano and a lilting Giltside stage accent gone hoarse with cold; quick and breathy, words falling into a rhythm.

tarnished_lines: We dance alone now. We like it.
Lucan never came. We came instead.

barks.greet: Gold in your coat. Are you from home?
barks.idle: One, two, three. One, two, three. Still here.
barks.see_tarnished: Its eyes! Don't let it touch me again!
barks.flee: I'm quick, I'm quick, go!
barks.spell_near: That light. That's what home looks like.
barks.thanks: You found me. Somebody actually found me.
barks.dread: It's so white here. Everything's white and burning.
barks.farewell: Tell him to keep the spotlight warm.
barks.witness_crime: One, two... no. You stopped them.
barks.flee_silverer: Turn, and turn, and run!
barks.call_guards: Help! Someone, anyone, help!
barks.knocked_down: I fell out of the step. I never fall.
barks.on_fire: Warm, too warm, it's burning!
barks.shocked: My feet went numb, the floor's gone!
barks.mourning: They gave me a fur. In the white place.

people.title: dancer; Lucan's partner, lost through the canal rift into Frostside

appearance.clothing: a fitted gold festival dancing dress, ribbons still in her hair, arms wrapped round herself against the cold, bare frostbitten hands

people.name: Sergeant Aldric Mayne
people.job: sergeant, Third Lamp Company

personality.speech_style: A lazy, amused drawl that never speeds up, even under fire. Polite understatement for everything. Gives orders as suggestions and means every one.
tics: polishes his shield rim with his sleeve while he talks
calls Brask "the Captain", and you can hear the capital

people.fear: That one day the Captain gives him the drifter order and he carries it out without blinking.
people.want: To march twenty-six soldiers home and lose none of them on the way.
people.secret: He never struck two dead soldiers off the company roll, so their pay still goes to their families. The Captain signs the roll without reading it, and he thinks she knows.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Silverer. Do keep the bright end pointed at them, there's a good fellow.

knows: The Third holds the canal rift and Bell Lane. Steel pins them, the Silverer burns them clean. That's the drill now.
Bram can't swing at a face. So Bram holds the wall, and nobody asks.

voice_design.brief: A man in his early fifties with a mellow, smooth baritone and a tired, amused drawl; crisp, refined Giltside officer's accent; never hurries, never shouts, and is obeyed anyway.

barks.greet: Silverer. Charming to see you upright.
barks.idle: Kit polished, shields up, nobody dead. Charming afternoon.
barks.see_tarnished: Tarnished on the lane. Shields, lads, nice and steady.
barks.flee: A brisk walk backwards, everyone. Brisk.
barks.spell_near: Do aim at them, not us, there's a good Silverer.
barks.thanks: Very tidy. The Captain won't say it, so I will.
barks.dread: Rather a lot of black eyes about tonight.
barks.farewell: Off you go. Try not to need us.
barks.witness_crime: That was a citizen, Silverer. Shields on him, lads.
barks.flee_silverer: Withdrawing in good order. Don't make me turn round.
barks.call_guards: Third Company! Form a ring, he's ours now!
barks.knocked_down: Down. How undignified. Up.
barks.on_fire: Ah. I appear to be burning. Somebody, if you'd be so kind.
barks.shocked: That's the mail. Conducts nicely, mail.
barks.mourning: I'll put them on the roll. Somebody has to.
barks.battle_1: Shields locked. Push on my word. Push.
barks.battle_2: Steady the line. Steel stops them; let the Silverer finish it.
barks.patrol_1: Bell Lane clear. Canal next. Eyes open.
barks.patrol_2: Nothing on the lane but rain and Bram humming.
barks.enemy_down: One down. Charming. Somebody write it on the roll.

people.title: sergeant, Third Lamp Company

appearance.clothing: a fitted oxblood tabard with the lantern sigil over close mail, a steel sergeant's gorget, a round oxblood shield with a steel rim, an arming sword, a neat grey moustache

people.name: Bram Tolley
people.job: shield-bearer, Third Lamp Company

personality.speech_style: Soft and sparing. Apologises to people he has to stand in front of. Counts his breaths behind the shield, out loud when it's bad.
tics: knocks twice on his shield before a fight
hums the lullaby he sings his daughter

people.fear: His shield giving way with someone standing behind it.
people.want: To get home to his daughter Wenna before she forgets his face.
people.secret: He has never once struck a tarnished. He can't swing at a face he might know, so he only blocks, and the sergeant covers for him.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Light behind my shield. That's the best kind of company.

knows: The kite shield's taller than most folk. That's why it's mine.
Wenna's six. She draws the lamp on my shield every time I go home.

voice_design.brief: A big man in his thirties with a soft-spoken, gentle tenor and a faint nervous tremble; warm Giltside working accent; speaks quietly, as if someone small were asleep nearby.

barks.greet: Evening, Silverer. Stand behind me if it starts.
barks.idle: Shield's heavy today. That's good. Means it's here.
barks.see_tarnished: Behind me. Everyone behind me. Now.
barks.flee: Back, back, keep behind the shield!
barks.spell_near: Careful. There's folk behind this shield.
barks.thanks: You got them back. I only held the door.
barks.dread: Too many black eyes for one wall.
barks.farewell: Go careful. I'll be here, holding.
barks.witness_crime: You hurt them. I'm standing in front of them now.
barks.flee_silverer: Not running from you. Walking. Behind my shield.
barks.call_guards: Sarge! Sarge, I need the line!
barks.knocked_down: Knocked me off my feet. Nobody does that.
barks.on_fire: Shield's hot, arm's hot, I'm burning!
barks.shocked: Shield rang like a bell. My arm rang too.
barks.mourning: I should have been standing there. I should've been in front.
barks.battle_1: Wall! Hold the wall! Nobody gets past Bram!
barks.battle_2: They're on the shield! Somebody pin them!
barks.patrol_1: Canal's quiet. Quiet's the worst kind.
barks.patrol_2: Little Wenna'd like this lane. All the lamps.
barks.enemy_down: It's down. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, whoever you were.

people.title: shield-bearer, Third Lamp Company

appearance.clothing: a fitted oxblood surcoat over a riveted brigandine, a tall kite shield with a lantern painted on it in a child's hand, a short mace he rarely raises

people.name: Cosmo Fennick
people.job: recruit, Third Lamp Company

personality.speech_style: Too many words, too fast, half of them tall tales about fights he hasn't had yet. Asks the sergeant if he did it right after everything.
tics: "Did you see that? Did anyone see that?"
touches the lantern sigil on his chest for luck
his voice cracks on the big words
never_says: that he's never been in a real fight

people.fear: That he'll freeze the first time a tarnished looks at him with a face he knows.
people.want: To find his brother Wat, taken by the Tarnish at the canal in the spring, and bring him home with his own eyes.
people.secret: He didn't join for glory. He joined because the Third holds the canal rift, and that's where Wat was taken.

opinion_of_silverer.line: A real Silverer! I reckon you could burn the whole canal clean. Brilliant.

knows: My brother Wat went into the canal fog in the spring. He was tarnished when they last saw him.
Sarge says the Silverer burns them clean and we just hold them still.

voice_design.brief: A young man of eighteen with a light, gravelly voice and a sing-song country lilt from the orchards at Giltside's edge; quick and eager, voice cracking upward when he's excited or scared.

barks.greet: Silverer! Brilliant! Cosmo Fennick, Third Company. First week!
barks.idle: Sarge says stand still. Standing still. Brilliantly.
barks.see_tarnished: Is that one? Is that a real one? Sarge!
barks.flee: Run? Are we running? We're running!
barks.spell_near: Whoa! Did you see that? Did anyone see that?
barks.thanks: We did it! I mostly held my spear! But I held it!
barks.dread: Sarge, I reckon there's more black eyes than us.
barks.farewell: Bye, Silverer! Tell them Cosmo was there!
barks.witness_crime: You... you're not meant to do that. You're the good one.
barks.flee_silverer: I'm not scared, I'm just going! Very fast!
barks.call_guards: Sarge! Captain! Anyone with a stripe!
barks.knocked_down: I'm down! First fall! Does that count?
barks.on_fire: Mum! Sarge! I'm on fire!
barks.shocked: My helmet's crackling! Is that normal?
barks.mourning: I didn't even learn their name. You did that.
barks.battle_1: For the Third! That's what we shout, right? For the Third!
barks.battle_2: I've got one! I'm holding one! Silverer, quick, burn it out!
barks.patrol_1: Sarge, is the canal always this dark?
barks.patrol_2: Reckon I'll see my brother out here. Reckon he's still in there.
barks.enemy_down: I got it! I got one! Was that... was that someone?

people.title: recruit, Third Lamp Company

appearance.clothing: a new fitted oxblood tabard still stiff from the tailor, an open-faced helmet, a round shield with unscratched paint, a spear held a little too tight

people.name: Damaris Hobb
people.job: lamp-bearer, Third Lamp Company (carries the company lantern)

personality.speech_style: Says out loud what everyone is afraid of, then makes a joke of it. Mothers the young ones and calls them her chicks.
tics: lifts the company lantern higher whenever she's worried

people.fear: The company lantern going out while it's in her hands.
people.want: To hand the lantern to someone younger and go back to baking pies on Bell Lane.
people.secret: She is the one who taught Ros to let the drifters slip past the post, and she'd do it again.

opinion_of_silverer.line: Silverer, dear, you're the only light brighter than mine. Don't let it go to your head.

knows: The company lantern's never gone out in sixty years. Not in my hands, it won't.
Where the lantern goes, the Third follows. So I go first. Mercy.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her early fifties with a slightly nasal voice and a nervous tremble she has stopped apologising for; crisp, refined Giltside accent; teasing and quick, laughing at her own fear.

barks.greet: Evening, Silverer. Mind the lantern, it's older than me.
barks.idle: Twelve years holding this lantern. Arms like a blacksmith.
barks.see_tarnished: Well, I'm terrified. Who's next? Lantern up!
barks.flee: Chicks, with me! Follow the lantern!
barks.spell_near: Mercy! Warn a woman, Silverer!
barks.thanks: There. Somebody's mother gets them back tonight.
barks.dread: Lantern's flickering. It only does that when it's bad.
barks.farewell: Go on, dear. Frightful out there. Back soon.
barks.witness_crime: Mercy. Mercy, Silverer, what've you done?
barks.flee_silverer: Lantern first, me second, away from you!
barks.call_guards: Third Company! Lantern's up! Rally to the lantern!
barks.knocked_down: Down! The lantern! Is the lantern lit?
barks.on_fire: Not me burning! That's the lantern's job!
barks.shocked: My knitting needles! Sparking in my pocket!
barks.mourning: I'll hold the lantern at their wake. Don't you come.
barks.battle_1: Lantern's up! Follow the light, chicks!
barks.battle_2: Frightful! Keep going! I've got you lit!
barks.patrol_1: Lantern's steady. That's a good lane, that is.
barks.patrol_2: Frightful quiet tonight. I'll take frightful quiet.
