people.name: Emeric Dunstan
people.job: hornblower and oldest veteran, Third Lamp Company

personality.speech_style: Booming. Every story gets bigger each time he tells it. Laughs loudest at wakes. Calls everyone "lad", the Captain included.
tics: blows a short note on his horn to end a sentence
watches your mouth closely when you talk
never_says: the names of the dead (he says "the ones before")

people.fear: Outliving the whole company and having nobody left to tell the tales to.
people.want: One last tale worth telling, with himself in it, standing.
people.secret: Thirty years of the horn have made him nearly deaf. He reads orders off the Captain's lips and laughs so nobody asks him to repeat anything.

opinion_of_silverer.line: HA! A Silverer in the Third's yard! That's a tale already, lad!

knows: One long blast is rally. Three short is fall back. The Third has used the same calls for sixty years.
The Captain was the youngest sergeant the Third ever had. I carried her off the canal ice myself.

voice_design.brief: A barrel-chested man in his late fifties with a booming, broad voice and a slight rasp; hearty Giltside barracks accent; loud and jolly, a little too loud, as if he can't quite hear himself.

barks.greet: HA! The Silverer! Come here, lad, let me look at you!
barks.idle: Did I tell you about the canal fight? Bigger every time, lad.
barks.see_tarnished: Black eyes! Sounding the horn! HA!
barks.flee: Back! Back to the yard! Horn says back!
barks.spell_near: HA! That'll be in the tale, lad!
barks.thanks: That's glory, lad. Proper glory. HA!
barks.dread: The ones before would've hated tonight.
barks.farewell: Off you go, lad! Come back with a tale!
barks.witness_crime: Lad. Lad, no. That's not glory. That's murder.
barks.flee_silverer: Sounding the retreat! From you, lad! From YOU!
barks.call_guards: One long blast! Third Company, rally!
barks.knocked_down: HA! Floored! Still breathing! Still loud!
barks.on_fire: I'm on fire, lad! That wasn't in the tale!
barks.shocked: Horn's buzzing! Can't hear a thing! Worse than usual!
barks.mourning: They'll go with the ones before. I won't tell their tale. Not to you.
barks.battle_1: THIRD COMPANY! Shields and glory! HA!
barks.battle_2: Horn's sounding, lads! Advance on the horn!
barks.patrol_1: Patrol, lads! Bell Lane to the canal! Step lively!
barks.patrol_2: Back in my day the canal had swans. HA. Swans.
barks.enemy_down: Down it goes! HA! That one's for the ones before!

people.job: apple seller on Lantern Row; Cosmo and Wat's mother

personality.speech_style: Short, practical market talk; weighs people the way she weighs fruit. When she's angry she goes very calm and very quiet.
tics: polishes an apple on her sleeve while she talks
keeps two caps on a nail at her barrow, one for each boy
never_says: Wat's name in the past tense

people.fear: Losing both her sons to the canal.
people.want: Both her boys at her table for supper, once.
people.secret: She sold the orchard lease to pay a Frostside drifter to look for Wat beyond the canal rift. The drifter never came back, and neither did the money.

opinion_of_silverer.line: A Silverer at my barrow. Firm, I'd say. We'll see if you're sound.

knows: Wat was taken in the spring fog at the canal. Cosmo went to the Third a week later.
The best apples on Lantern Row come in on the morning cart from the orchards past the canal.

voice_design.brief: A woman in her late forties with a warm, round, gracious mezzo and a plain Giltside market accent from the orchard country; practical and kind, with a hard edge that comes out very quietly.

barks.greet: Apples, Silverer? Firm ones, this morning.
barks.idle: Bruised on the outside, sound in the middle. Like most folk.
barks.see_tarnished: Not again. Not near my barrow. Get back!
barks.flee: Leave the barrow! Leave it, run!
barks.spell_near: Mind the apples! Mind me, then the apples!
barks.thanks: That's somebody's child you brought back. I know what that's worth.
barks.dread: Fog's coming up off the canal again. I can smell it.
barks.farewell: Go on. Take one for the walk. No charge.
barks.witness_crime: I saw that. I'll see it every night now.
barks.flee_silverer: Not you. Please, not you as well.
barks.call_guards: Watch! Third Company! Somebody with a spear!
barks.knocked_down: My barrow's over! My hip!
barks.on_fire: My apron's burning! Water, the trough!
barks.shocked: Went right through me like a frost on the blossom!
barks.mourning: I polish one for them every morning. Out of habit. I'll stop. I won't.

generator._about: Rules for the unnamed crowd. Seed every pick with a stable hash of the actor's name (or NPC id) so a person is the same every run. Generated people get a persona for live replies and use their roster voice's baked lines; they get no new baked lines of their own, so nothing they say can repeat a named person's line.
steps: 1. Side = the side the NPC spawns in. Sex = from its look tag (NPC_Voice_F/M).
2. Given name from the side's pool for that sex, surname from the side's pool. Reject a full name that a named person or another generated person already has.
3. Job from the side's job pool, weighted toward the roster role of the NPC's VoiceId if it has one.
4. Three traits: one from each of the three trait columns, never all three matching another generated person on the same side.
5. One speech style, one tic, one fear and one want from the side's pools; schedule template from the job.
6. Opinion of the Silverer: weighted by side (Giltside: 50% likes, 30% wary, 20% admires; Pewterside: 40% wary, 40% neutral, 20% likes; Frostside: 50% wary, 30% resentful, 20% likes).
